Hi team,

Attaching an initial sketch of the deployment boundary for Sentinel's Dedicated cluster request. This is the first pass that separates:
- Control plane (management, provisioning, KMS integration)
- Data plane (inference runtime, model artifacts, ephemeral KV cache)
- Customer tenant overlay (VPC peering + service account mapping)

Key asks:
1) Sentinel: confirm the highlighted egress endpoints you need (line items on page 3).
2) Auditors/SIG: if you want explicit wire-level diagrams (BGP/NAT details) I can add that as a supplement.

Attachments: redwood-network-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram, annotated), control-matrix-soc2.csv (controls mapping)

Thanks,
Ben

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel deployment boundary summary and initial artifacts

Thanks Ben — good start. A couple of clarifying items from product/architecture perspective: 

- For Dedicated we enforce isolation at two layers: 1) hyperplane (namespace/container level + kernel networking rules) and 2) network demarcation (dedicated subnets + dedicated egress paths). The diagram should call out which controls are OS-level vs network-level.
- Can you add a short note on the control plane flow for model updates (who pushes, signed artifact flow, KMS enveloping) — auditors often want the chain-of-custody outlined in the same packet.
- For Sentinel's ask, we need to ensure the diagram explicitly shows the optional VPC peering vs private endpoint option for customers (they choose one).

If you can attach the SIG/CAIQ mapping in spreadsheet form, I'll run a quick pass to mark which ops artifacts map to each SIG question.

Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Product, Redwood Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Thanks — attaching the completed SIG spreadsheet and a short narrative. A few notes that will help the SOC 2 pack: 
- Our procurement security team requires a clear mapping of which egress IPs will be reachable from the deployed runtime for model telemetry/metrics. The diagram page 4 helps but we need canonical CIDR lists.
- For the model update flow: we plan to deliver a signed tarball over an authenticated channel into the control plane. We need confirmation that Redwood's KMS envelope will be used (we prefer customer-managed keys but can accept Redwood-managed for the pilot).

- CIDR list: Ben will export the canonical egress CIDRs and add as an appendix to the diagram (we typically publish a short list per-region).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private deployments; I'll add the KMS flow diagram into the packet and mark the SIG questions that this addresses (Key custody + rotation).
- Next step: I'll produce a single "SOC2 + SIG packet" zip that includes redwood-network-diagram-v2.pdf, sentinel-questionnaire-sig.xlsx (annotated), control-matrix-soc2.csv, and a short mapping doc. Expect that by COB Monday.
